text.description: Whole JSON lines, each ended by a line feed. Only the first page starts with the header.

next.description: What to ask for the next page with ([`SessionExport::after`]); absent when the export is complete.

program.description: The program: a path, or a name looked up on the `PATH` where it runs, the spec's own `PATH` when its environment sets one.

args.description: Its arguments, one element each, never re-split by a shell.

remove_environment.description: Variables taken out of the spawner's own environment before `environment` is set.

terminal.description: A terminal of this size for its input and output, standard error included; plain pipes when absent.

os.description: The operating system they run on, spelled as Rust's `std::env::consts::OS` spells it (`windows`, `linux`, `macos`, `android`): which rules their paths follow.

arch.description: Their processor, spelled as `std::env::consts::ARCH` spells it.

local.description: Whether they run on the host's own machine, sharing its files and paths.

separate_error.description: Whether a spec may keep standard error apart from standard output.

survives_link_loss.description: Whether a process keeps running while the link to it is down, its output kept for when it comes back.

kills_escaped.description: Whether [`SpawnedProcess::kill`] also reaches the processes that left the program's process group or session; when not, those escape it.

ends_with_host.description: Whether a process's tree ends when the host dies without killing it (its group or job, at least); when not, it outlives the host.

running.description: Whether it still runs; neither `code` nor `signal` is set while it does.

code.description: Its exit code, when it exited by itself.

signal.description: The signal that ended it, on Unix.

up.description: Whether it is up now. A local process's link is always up.

drops.description: How many times it has gone down since the process started: a reader that sees the count grow knows its output paused.
